description: Gold is a chemical element with atomic number 79 and symbol Au. In its pure form, it is a bright metallic-yellow, dense, soft, malleable, and ductile metal that is a transition metal and one of the noble metals, ranking second lowest in the reactivity series with only platinum being less reactive.
uses: Gold has been used for coinage, jewelry, and works of art throughout recorded history. Its chief industrial use is in corrosion-resistant electrical connectors in computerized devices due to its conductivity and resistance to corrosion, and it is also used in infrared shielding, colored glass production, gold leafing, tooth restoration, and in the drug auranofin for treating rheumatoid arthritis.
characteristics: Gold is the most malleable metal and can be beaten into extremely thin sheets or drawn into single-atom-width wires without noticeable hardening. It has a density of 19.3 g/cm³, is a good conductor of heat and electricity, and possesses a distinctive reddish-yellow color due to relativistic quantum chemical effects. Gold is resistant to most acids except aqua regia and dissolves in alkaline cyanide solutions and mercury, and it does not react with oxygen at any temperature.
